Erin (Sales): quick heads-up — prospect (regional bank) asked during POC kickoff: what is our incident response / breach notification timeline? they specifically called out GDPR and local banking regs, want confirmed SLA for notifications.

Mike (Security): short answer: we don't give a one-size 24h guarantee across the board. typical approach: detection/triage within hours, confirmed incidents involving personal data — notify customers per regulator timelines (GDPR: 72h for data breaches). for severe availability/security incidents we aim to provide an initial customer notification ASAP (usually within ~4–8 hours) and a follow-up with details within 72h. we can also provide interim updates.

Erin (Sales): ok — customer asked if we can put 24h in the SOW for POC. they want faster than GDPR. can we do that?

Mike (Security): we can agree to contractually shorter notification windows but only after legal review and scoped controls. 24h for confirmed breaches is aggressive; it requires dedicated on-call, direct incident hooks, and routing guarantees. for POC we can offer our standard timeline and an escalation path.

Jules (Solutions): for the POC we can enable verbose audit logs, request/response traces, and retention to help them investigate. can also run the POC in Private mode (VPC) if they need isolation — that reduces cross-tenant impact risk.

Erin (Sales): they asked about evidence chain / forensics: how long do we keep logs and can we hand them over?

Mike (Security): we retain platform audit logs by default for 90 days. for Dedicated/Private customers we can extend retention or provide snapshots on request (we typically keep forensic snapshots for 30 days after an incident unless otherwise contracted). we maintain chain-of-custody and can hand over logs/forensic exports under NDA and appropriate legal process.

Sarah (Legal): pointer — we shouldn't promise log handing without an MSA addendum and evidence-request process. also note: obligation to notify regulators/third parties is ultimately the customer's responsibility in many cases, but we cooperate and provide required data per contract and law. I'll draft wording.

Erin (Sales): can you paste a short suggested clause I can give the customer now?

Sarah (Legal): here's a starter clause they can review (won't be final):

```
Notification and Cooperation. Redwood Inference will notify Customer of a confirmed security incident affecting Customer data as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation when required by applicable data protection law. For critical incidents impacting service availability or integrity, Redwood will provide an initial notification to Customer as soon as practicable (typically within 4–8 hours of detection) and will provide timely updates. Redwood will cooperate with Customer and, where permitted by law, provide logs, forensic exports, and other evidence under an executed non-disclosure and data transfer agreement. Specific notification SLAs and evidence retention requirements may be set forth in an addendum to the Master Services Agreement.
```

Mike (Security): addendum options we normally offer for enterprise: dedicated SIRT contact, 24/7 escalation phone, accelerated notification SLA, longer log retention (365 days), and live-streamed forensic access for emergencies. Those require extra ops/commitments.

Erin (Sales): also asked about SIG/CAIQ / vendor risk review — timeline for us to complete that?

Mike (Security): standard answers for SIG/CAIQ take ~3 business days. full custom responses or evidence packages ~7–10 business days. if they need signed attestation or SOC2 artifacts we'll coordinate with Compliance — that can take up to 2 weeks to gather redacted artifacts.

Jules (Solutions): actionables for POC: enable full audit logging, set retention to 180 days for the trial, add SIRT contact to config, and capture the customer contact details for notifications. I can spin that up today if we have approval.

Erin (Sales): customer wants the SIRT contact and an on-call number in the SOW for POC. can we provide a placeholder?

Sarah (Legal): we can provide a generic SIRT contact + Incident Response email. Final on-call number needs legal OK — will avoid a fixed personal number in docs. use: security-incidents@redwood.ai (placeholder) and escalate via the signatory in the addendum.

IncidentBot: Deployment note — POC project "RB-POC-489": audit logging enabled, retention set to 180d, dedicated S3 snapshot schedule configured.

Mike (Security): I'll prepare a 1-page IR summary to send to the prospect: detection → triage → customer notification → remediation → postmortem. will include expected timelines and what we need from them (contact, scope, authority to request logs).

Erin (Sales): perfect. next steps: 1) Sarah to send clause + any redlines (ETA 2 business days) 2) Mike to produce IR one-pager and SIG/CAIQ timeline (ETA 2 business days) 3) Jules to enable logging + retention for POC (today) 4) Erin to share prospect contact and confirm whether they want Private deployment. I'll update customer after we have the one-pager. :thumbsup:

Sarah (Legal): noted. I'll add a short paragraph about regulator notification limits — we can suggest: "Customer is responsible for regulator filing unless Redwood is required by law to notify; Redwood will assist and coordinate."

Jules (Solutions): set. ping me the account id and I'll confirm the POC settings.

Erin (Sales): sending account id in DM. thanks everyone! :pray:
